title: Perimeter and Area of Plane Shapes
seo_title: Perimeter and Area – Primary 5 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the perimeter of regular and irregular plane shapes; find the area of squares, rectangles and composite shapes; solve problems on area and perimeter. (summary of the NERDC Primary 5 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 maths worksheets on perimeter and area: rectangles, squares and composite shapes, estimating area and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Perimeter: add the sides. Area: length × breadth.
key_sub: Area is in square units (cm², m²).
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Perimeter is the distance all the way round a shape: add the lengths of all the sides.
  • Area is the space inside a shape. Area of a rectangle = length × breadth; of a square = side × side.
  • Split a composite (L-shaped) shape into rectangles, find each area and add.

Examples

Example

Rectangle 12 m by 7 m

Perimeter = 2 × (12 + 7)

Area = 12 × 7

Answer: 38 m and 84 m²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up perimeter and areaPerimeter is a length (m); area is in square units (m²).
Adding only two sidesA rectangle has four sides.
Counting a side twice in a composite shapeMark the sides as you add them.

faq.q: Can two shapes have the same area but different perimeters?
Why is area in square units?
faq.a: We count how many unit squares cover the shape.

items.e: Area of a rectangle = length × width: 8 × 5 = 40 cm². 26 cm would be the perimeter.

items.q: The area of this rectangle is 48 cm². What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Length × width = area, so width = area ÷ length: 48 ÷ 8 = 6 cm. Check: 8 × 6 = 48 cm².

items.q: The area of this rectangle is 63 m². What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Length × width = area, so width = area ÷ length: 63 ÷ 9 = 7 m. Check: 9 × 7 = 63 m².

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 84 cm². It is 12 cm long. How wide is it?
items.e: Length × width = area, so width = area ÷ length: 84 ÷ 12 = 7 cm. Check: 12 × 7 = 84 cm².

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 90 m². It is 15 m long. How wide is it?
items.e: Length × width = area, so width = area ÷ length: 90 ÷ 15 = 6 m. Check: 15 × 6 = 90 m².

items.q: Which rectangle has the largest area?
items.e: Work out length × width for each: 10 × 3 = 30, 6 × 6 = 36, 8 × 4 = 32, 11 × 2 = 22. The largest is 6 cm by 6 cm (36 cm²). The longest perimeter does not always give the largest area.

items.q: Which rectangle has the smallest area?
items.e: Work out length × width for each: 5 × 5 = 25, 8 × 3 = 24, 13 × 2 = 26, 7 × 4 = 28. The smallest is 8 m by 3 m (24 m²). Do not compare the side lengths: work out each area.

items.q: Which rectangle has the largest area?
items.e: Work out length × width for each: 9 × 5 = 45, 12 × 3 = 36, 7 × 7 = 49, 15 × 2 = 30. The largest is 7 m by 7 m (49 m²). The longest perimeter does not always give the largest area.

items.q: Which rectangle has the largest area?
items.e: Work out length × width for each: 14 × 4 = 56, 9 × 7 = 63, 16 × 3 = 48, 10 × 6 = 60. The largest is 9 cm by 7 cm (63 cm²). The longest perimeter does not always give the largest area.

items.q: A leaf is drawn on a grid. Each square is 1 cm². It covers 14 whole squares and 9 squares that are half or more covered. 6 more squares are less than half covered. Estimate its area.
items.e: Count whole squares and squares half or more covered: 14 + 9 = 23 cm². Leave out the 6 squares that are less than half covered.

items.q: A puddle is drawn on a grid. Each square is 1 cm². It covers 21 whole squares and 8 squares that are half or more covered. 7 more squares are less than half covered. Estimate its area.
items.e: Count whole squares and squares half or more covered: 21 + 8 = 29 cm². Leave out the 7 squares that are less than half covered.

items.q: A pond is drawn on a grid. Each square is 1 m². It covers 32 whole squares and 11 squares that are half or more covered. 9 more squares are less than half covered. Estimate its area.
items.e: Count whole squares and squares half or more covered: 32 + 11 = 43 m². Leave out the 9 squares that are less than half covered.

items.q: A footprint is drawn on a grid. Each square is 1 cm². It covers 18 whole squares and 7 squares that are half or more covered. 10 more squares are less than half covered. Estimate its area.
items.e: Count whole squares and squares half or more covered: 18 + 7 = 25 cm². Leave out the 10 squares that are less than half covered.

items.q: A map of an island is drawn on a grid. Each square is 1 cm². It covers 26 whole squares and 12 squares that are half or more covered. 8 more squares are less than half covered. Estimate its area.
items.e: Count whole squares and squares half or more covered: 26 + 12 = 38 cm². Leave out the 8 squares that are less than half covered.

items.q: You estimate the area of an irregular shape on a squared grid. Which squares do you count?
c: Whole and half or more covered
items.e: Count every whole square, and count a square as 1 if half or more of it is covered. Leave out squares that are less than half covered. The parts you count and leave out roughly balance.

items.q: Abdullahi’s bedroom floor is a rectangle 4 m long and 3 m wide. What area of carpet does he need to cover it?
items.e: Covering a floor is area: 4 × 3 = 12 m².

items.q: Gbenga’s family puts a fence round their rectangular garden. It is 15 m long and 8 m wide. How much fence do they need?
items.e: The fence goes along all 4 sides: 15 + 8 + 15 + 8 = 46 m.

items.q: A classroom floor is 9 m long and 7 m wide. What is the area of the floor?
items.e: Length × width: 9 × 7 = 63 m².

items.q: This is the plan of an L-shaped hall. What area of carpet covers the whole floor?
items.e: Split into two rectangles: 4 × 3 = 12 and 10 × 5 = 50. Total: 12 + 50 = 62 m².

items.q: Obinna’s garden is 8 m by 6 m. Zainab’s garden is 7 m by 7 m. Which garden has the larger area, and by how much?
items.e: Obinna: 8 × 6 = 48 m². Zainab: 7 × 7 = 49 m². 49 − 48 = 1 m². The perimeters are both 28 m, but the areas are different.

items.q: A square playground has a perimeter of 64 m. What is its area?
items.e: Each side: 64 ÷ 4 = 16 m. Area: 16 × 16 = 256 m².

items.q: A rectangular flower bed has a perimeter of 34 m. It is 11 m long. How wide is it?
items.e: The two long sides make 2 × 11 = 22 m. 34 − 22 = 12 m for the two short sides, so each is 12 ÷ 2 = 6 m.

items.q: A rectangular poster has an area of 600 cm². It is 30 cm wide. How tall is it?
items.e: Area = width × height, so height = 600 ÷ 30 = 20 cm. Check: 30 × 20 = 600 cm².

items.q: A patio is 6 m long and 4 m wide. Square paving slabs are 1 m by 1 m and come in packs of 5. How many packs are needed?
items.e: Area: 6 × 4 = 24 m², so 24 slabs. 24 ÷ 5 = 4 remainder 4. 4 packs are not enough, so 5 packs.

items.q: A rectangular field is 25 m long and 18 m wide. A fence goes all the way round, except for a gate 3 m wide. How much fence is needed?
items.e: Perimeter: 25 + 18 + 25 + 18 = 86 m. No fence across the gate: 86 − 3 = 83 m.

items.q: A football pitch is 100 m long and 64 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Length × width: 100 × 64 = 6,400 m².

items.q: Uju is making a rabbit pen with an area of 36 m². It could be 9 m by 4 m or 6 m by 6 m. Which pen needs less fence?
items.e: Both have an area of 36 m². Fence: 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26 m and 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24 m. The square needs less fence.

items.q: Chinedu has 20 m of fence to make a rectangular vegetable patch. Which patch has the largest area?
items.e: All four use 20 m of fence. Areas: 9 × 1 = 9 m², 8 × 2 = 16 m², 7 × 3 = 21 m², 5 × 5 = 25 m². The square has the largest area.

items.q: A wall is 5 m long and 3 m high. It has a door 1 m wide and 2 m high. What area of wall needs painting?
items.e: Wall: 5 × 3 = 15 m². Door: 1 × 2 = 2 m². Take away the door: 15 − 2 = 13 m².

items.q: A classroom display board is 120 cm long and 90 cm wide. What is its area?
items.e: Length × width: 120 × 90 = 10,800 cm². Tip: 12 × 9 = 108, then × 100.

items.q: Room A is 5 m by 4 m. Room B is 6 m by 3 m. Which is true?
items.e: Areas: 5 × 4 = 20 m² and 6 × 3 = 18 m², so A is larger. Perimeters: both 18 m.

items.q: A lawn is 12 m by 8 m. In the middle is a square pond with sides of 3 m. What area of grass is there?
items.e: Lawn: 12 × 8 = 96 m². Pond: 3 × 3 = 9 m². Grass: 96 − 9 = 87 m².
Whole squares: 9. Squares half or more covered: 5. Estimate: 9 + 5 = 14 m².

items.q: A rectangle is 12 cm by 6 cm. A square has the same perimeter. What is the area of the square?
items.e: Perimeter of the rectangle: 12 + 6 + 12 + 6 = 36 cm. Side of the square: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm. Area: 9 × 9 = 81 cm².

items.q: Temi’s bedroom floor is a rectangle 4 m long and 3 m wide. What area of carpet does she need to cover it?
items.e: Covering a floor is area: 4 × 3 = 12 m².
